title: New Hope Garden Trip
description:
Join us to visit Bowman's Hill Wildflower Preserve and explore over 130 acres of beautiful native plants, peaceful woodland trails, and scenic outdoor views perfect for a relaxing day in nature.  Optional add on : The New Hope Railroad (starting at $35) for a charming rail ride through the Pennsylvania countryside or explore the town of New Hope. Tickets for the railroad are not covered by Outdoor Adventure, and must be purchased on your own. 
   
 How do I sign-up? 
 
 Register  here  or in the Student Rec Center main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340). 
 Cost for Students $10 
 
   
 Where and when? 
 
 October 17th, 2026 
 9am-6pm 
 Bus leaves from Student Recreation Center 
 
   
 What to bring:  Bring lunch, water, sneakers and a sense of adventure!  
   
 Potential Hazards:  Unpredictable weather changes, sunburn/heat exhaustion, dehydration, allergic reactions/poisonous plants, insect bites, and injury by running, including sprains, lacerations, abrasions and fractures.

title: Free Swim Lessons *Beginner*
description:

title: What is a Man?
organization: Lambda Sigma Upsilon Latino Fraternity, Inc.
description: What is a Man? is a real and open dialogue centered on the stigmatization of men and the expectations placed on masculinity. This space explores how societal pressures often force men to suppress emotion, struggle in silence, and avoid vulnerability. Through honest conversation, we aim to break down those barriers and address men’s mental health in a meaningful way. It’s a judgment-free environment that encourages reflection, healing, and connection, reminding everyone that redefining strength starts with being able to speak, feel, and be heard.

title: NASO General Body Meeting
description: Join us for the Native African Student Organization's General Body Meeting! This is a space where we come together to celebrate and explore the richness of African cultures, while also connecting with other cultures from around the world. At each meeting, we'll engage in lively discussions, learn about Africa’s diverse history, traditions, and current events, and empower each other to understand and embrace our heritage. Whether you're looking to deepen your cultural knowledge, make meaningful connections, or simply have fun with fellow students who share a passion for Africa and global cultures, this is the place to be! Let’s build a supportive community, amplify African voices on campus, and create lasting friendships. All are welcome, come, learn, share, and connect!

title: I am Jane Doe
description: I Am Jane Doe  is a collaborative program presented by The Office of Community Resilience and Officer Wellness, Advocacy and Outreach and Greek Life to raise awareness about sexual assault, support survivors, and foster meaningful conversations about consent, safety, and accountability. Inspired by the Silent Witness tradition, the program allows us to shed light on stories that often do not receive the attention they deserve and the difficulty survivors face when reporting. This program provides an opportunity for our community to engage thoughtfully in conversations surrounding sexual violence and its impact on individuals and campus communities.

title: Information Session: Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group
description:
Are you a graduate student working on a journal article for publication? Learn more about the Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group! 
 This writing group will run over 13 weeks during the Spring semester (January - April 2027), with a week off in March. Weekly topics will include: publication venues, selecting a journal, writing your argument, literature review, citation management and more. We will use Wendy Laura Belcher’s  Writing Your Journal Article in Twelve Weeks  to guide the discussions and work.  
 Register to attend this Zoom information session where we will discuss how the program will run, the expected time commitment, and answer any other questions you may have. Please contact cwe@montclair.edu with any questions. A limited number of seats are available. 
 Sponsored by the Center for Writing Excellence and the University Libraries. 
 Register Here: https://montclair.libcal.com/event/17747729

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support! 
 All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program. 
 Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair. 
 
 Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least  $20.26  and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe.  
 For a gift of  $40 , celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord. 
 
 How do I get my customized philanthropy cord? 
 Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up: 
 
 Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby 
 Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby 
 Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby 
 
 Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement. 
 Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward! For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week.  
 To Participate : RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set! 
 Requirements: 
 
 Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate. 
 Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this  link . 
 Once certified, email your certification to  foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org  to confirm your eligibility to participate. 
 
 Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation! *Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week.  
 To Participate : RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set! 
 Requirements: 
 
 Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate. 
 Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this   link . 
 Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate. 
 
 Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation! *Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support! 
 All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program. 
 Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair. 
 
 Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least  $20.26  and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe.  
 For a gift of  $40 , celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord. 
 
 How do I get my customized philanthropy cord? 
 Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up: 
 
 Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby 
 Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby 
 Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby 
 
 Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement. 
 Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward! For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.

 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . title: The American Experiment: Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss Information, Power, and Democracy: The First Amendment. 
 The First Amendment is the cornerstone of American democracy because it guarantees the fundamental freedoms required for citizens to govern themselves, including freedom of speech, freedom of the press, and freedom of assembly.  Citizens need access to open debate, diverse viewpoints, and accurate information in order to make informed decisions. These freedoms also protect unpopular and minority opinions and act as a check on the state from censoring speech or controlling what people learn, think, and say.  This lecture examines the foundational freedoms of the First Amendment and how they are applied to contemporary American democratic life, including: the impact of money on expression, the role of new media and corporate media, the role of the press in investigating and disseminating information, the right to protest as a form of assembly and expression, and the challenges posed by misinformation, disinformation, polarization, fragmented media audiences, and declining public trust. At its center is a fundamental question for American democracy: What are the inherent rights and responsibilities of freedom of expression in a democratic society?

title: Midterms Election Watch Party, Pizza & Power: Watch Democracy Unfold Live!
description:
Join us for an exciting Midterm Election Night Party on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, from 7 to 10 p.m. in the Fish Bowl, located in the School of Communication and Media lobby! 
 Come together with members of the campus community to watch the midterm election results unfold in real time. Follow the action and see who will prevail in New Jersey’s 12 U.S. House of Representatives districts, while also keeping an eye on other key races from across the country. 
 Hosted by the Office of Civic and Voter Engagement, the Department of Political Science and Law, the Political Science Club, and the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, the event will offer a lively and welcoming space to discuss the races, exchange insights, and experience democracy in action. 
 Whether you closely follow politics or simply want to enjoy the excitement of Election Night, this is a great opportunity to connect with others over pizza, conversation, and live results. Bring your friends and join us for an engaging evening as the nation decides the makeup of the next Congress!

title: Accounting Society - Wiss & Company
description: Wiss & Company LLP is a top 100 U.S. accounting and advisory firm founded in 1969. Headquartered in Florham Park, New Jersey, the firm operates additional offices in Flemington, New York City, and Boca Raton. Under the leadership of CEO Paul Peterson, a specialized team of roughly 450 employees serves middle-market businesses and private clients. Their comprehensive services include full-scale accounting, audit assurance, strategic tax planning, and outsourced fractional CFO solutions. Furthermore, Wiss Private Client Advisors delivers specialized wealth management and estate planning services. Finally, the firm drives business modernization through targeted process automation and AI-driven data intelligence.

title: 1st International Symposium of Latino Oral History
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
Join us for the  First International Symposium of Latino Oral History, “Listening as Resistance: Oral History, Memory and the Latino Experience”  taking place virtually on  November 6–7 . This two-day symposium will bring together scholars, students, educators, writers, and community members to explore the power of  oral history and Latino storytelling  as tools for preserving lived experiences, amplifying voices, and challenging dominant historical narratives. 
 We are honored to welcome acclaimed  writer, journalist, and University of California, Irvine professor Héctor Tobar  as our keynote speaker. 
 We invite participants to  submit an abstract  to present their work or  register to attend  and learn more about Latino storytelling and oral history practices. 
 Best paper will get a chance to be published in an academic journal. 
 Student registration is free. 
 Please register for the symposium with the link below: 
 https://montclair.co1. qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ cYowQOHwct2em0K 
 To submit an abstract:  
  https://montclair.co1. qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ 1N6j22Uqp6ulqiq

title: MoniCon
description:
MoniCon is a 2-Day Event providing the full fledged Convention experience right here on Montclair State University's Main Campus! Here at MoniCon we have a little something for everyone, so you will not want to miss out on this one of a kind event! Some of our many activities will include, Performances, Cosplay, Fursuits, a Game Room, an Artist Alley, Panels, Live Music, and more! MoniCon is an event made by students for everyone making it the perfect way to enjoy your weekend with an amazing experience! 
 .𖥔 ݁ ˖When & Where?.𖥔 ݁ ˖ MoniCon will take place from November 7th through November 8th 2026 on Montclair State University's Main Campus. The event will encompase both the Student Center and University Hall Buildings. MoniCon's hours of operations are 11:30AM-10:00PM on November 7th and 11:30PM-9:00PM on November 8th. 
 .𖥔 ݁ ˖How To Join?.𖥔 ݁ ˖ You can RSVP on any of the events labeled MoniCon, you do not have to RSVP to all of them in order to attend only one is ok! Event Passes will be eligable for purchase at the door and will be $10 for students and $20 for non students. If you would like to prepurchase a ticket online please check out our EventBrite to secure your spot early! 
 .𖥔 ݁ ˖About Us.𖥔 ݁ ˖ MoniCon is created as a community effort by the Montclair State Furry Club, Garfield Club, Aurora, Splatoon Club, Montclair Univeristy Gamers, Art Society, and Japan Club all in pursuits of making a unique and exciting event. If any of these clubs individually catch your eye check out their engage pages to learn more about the amazing oppertunities they individually bring to campus life.

title: Accounting Society - Nisivoccia
description: Nisivoccia LLP  is a prominent accounting, tax, and advisory firm founded in 1964 and based in New Jersey. Led by Managing Partner Nick Sarinelli, the firm operates out of offices including Mount Arlington, Bridgewater, and Newton. Their 140+ professionals provide financial statement audits, year-round tax planning, and strategic business advisory services. They specialize heavily in serving not-for-profit organizations, school districts, governmental bodies, and commercial real estate clients. Additionally, the firm offers specialized divisions for IT consulting, cybersecurity, and forensic fraud accounting. Over its 60-year history, Nisivoccia LLP has grown into a highly trusted regional partner for private and public entities.

title: Information Session: Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group
description:
Are you a graduate student working on a journal article for publication? Learn more about the Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group! 
 This writing group will run over 13 weeks during the Spring semester (January - April 2027), with a week off in March. Weekly topics will include: publication venues, selecting a journal, writing your argument, literature review, citation management and more. We will use Wendy Laura Belcher’s  Writing Your Journal Article in Twelve Weeks  to guide the discussions and work.  
 Register to attend this Zoom information session where we will discuss how the program will run, the expected time commitment, and answer any other questions you may have. Please contact cwe@montclair.edu with any questions. A limited number of seats are available.

title: Major & Career Exploration Talks: What We Wish We Knew Before Declaring!
description:
Not sure what major to choose or where your career path is headed? You’re not alone! Join us for  Major & Career Exploration Talks: What We Wish We Knew Before Declaring! , a dynamic panel event where upperclassmen students share their real, unfiltered experiences about choosing their majors and navigating their career journeys. Hear firsthand what they wish they knew before declaring, the challenges they faced, and how they found their passions. Whether you're feeling undecided, overwhelmed, or just curious about different paths, this event will give you insights, inspiration, and practical advice to help you make informed decisions. Don’t miss this opportunity to gain valuable perspectives and take the next step in your academic and career journey! * Food and refreshments will be served! 
 This workshop is presented by  The Discovery Program . To contact the Discovery Program, email us at  discoveryprogram@montclair.edu , or visit us at  montclair.edu/discovery-program .

title: Find the Sources You Need
description:
Learn where and how to search for books, articles, and more.  We’ll break down the differences between primary and secondary sources.  We'll discuss "credible sources," both those from scholarly (peer-reviewed) journals and those from other sources.  We'll also discuss, among other things, the differences between our two largest family of databases -- ProQuest and EBSCO. We want you to advance your searching skills so that you learn to have fun searching (a.k.a. researching). A perfect workshop if you’re new to college-level research or you just want to sharpen your skills before your next assignment. 
 Register Here:  https://montclair.libcal.com/event/17454788

title: Media, Identity, and Voice: From Radio Waves to Reels with New Jersey Hall of Fame
description: Join us for a hands-on workshop where educators explore how media shapes storytelling, identity, and representation. Through the New Jersey Hall of Fame, educators will explore exhibits spanning different historical media breakthroughs. From news anchor Connie Chung, to Thomas Edison’s invention of the first camera, to the iconic music of Whitney Houston— educators will become experts in multiple avenues of media production, bringing media literacy directly into their classroom. They will choose a project to develop, apply learned skills through Canva, and leave ready to support students through podcasts, reels, or digital shorts tied to New Jersey.

title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our  Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series , beginning  Monday, September 14 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. 
 Mondays, beginning September 14 5:30–7:30 p.m. Cole Hall, Room 141 10-week series 
 We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us.  Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

description:
Pre-Law Society’s newest sub-committee: Pre-Law Review!  
 A new student-run journal that aims to give Montclair State University Students the opportunity to explore current and historical legal issues through legal research, writing, and analysis. title: Accounting Society - Grant Thornton
description: Grant Thornton  is a leading global professional services network that provides comprehensive audit, tax, and advisory services to a diverse range of public and private organizations. Founded in Chicago in 1924, the network has expanded dramatically to include more than 80,000 professionals operating across 150 countries. Globally, it ranks as one of the largest accounting organizations by revenue, serving dynamic, mid-market businesses as well as massive multinational corporations.

title: NASO General Body Meeting
description: Join us for the Native African Student Organization's General Body Meeting! This is a space where we come together to celebrate and explore the richness of African cultures, while also connecting with other cultures from around the world. At each meeting, we'll engage in lively discussions, learn about Africa’s diverse history, traditions, and current events, and empower each other to understand and embrace our heritage. Whether you're looking to deepen your cultural knowledge, make meaningful connections, or simply have fun with fellow students who share a passion for Africa and global cultures, this is the place to be! Let’s build a supportive community, amplify African voices on campus, and create lasting friendships. All are welcome, come, learn, share, and connect!

title: Information Session: Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group
description:
Are you a graduate student working on a journal article for publication? Learn more about the Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group! 
 This writing group will run over 13 weeks during the Spring semester (January - April 2027), with a week off in March. Weekly topics will include: publication venues, selecting a journal, writing your argument, literature review, citation management and more. We will use Wendy Laura Belcher’s  Writing Your Journal Article in Twelve Weeks  to guide the discussions and work.  
 Register to attend this Zoom information session where we will discuss how the program will run, the expected time commitment, and answer any other questions you may have. Please contact cwe@montclair.edu with any questions. A limited number of seats are available. 
 Sponsored by the Center for Writing Excellence and the University Libraries. 
 Register Here: https://montclair.libcal.com/event/17747787

title: Cali Immersive Residency: The Hands Free & Dance Heginbotham —The Party Scene
description:
Exquisitely eclectic quartet  The Hands Free  and members of the fabulously whimsical  Dance Heginbotham  join forces in  The Party Scene . Inspired by  The Nutcracker  and your holiday office party, this music and dance extravaganza is part Drosselmeyer and part Turkey Lurkey Time. Lightly immersive and family-friendly, The Party Scene features student party guests from Montclair State University. All guests are encouraged to don impressively festive seasonal sweaters. 
 About The Hands Free:  The Hands Free is an acoustic quartet, bringing together the creative voices of composer/performers  James Moore  (guitar & banjo),  Caroline Shaw  (violin),  Nathan Koci  (accordion), and  Eleonore Oppenheim  (bass). Drawing from an eclectic array of influences in classical, jazz, and folk traditions, the group produces a unique and evocative blend of joyful melodies, lush sonic textures, and explosive improvisations. 
 About Dance Heginbotham:  Dance Heginbotham (DH) is a New York-based contemporary dance company committed to supporting, producing, and performing the work of choreographer  John Heginbotham . With an emphasis on collaboration, DH enriches national and international communities through its unique blend of inventive, thoughtful, and rigorous dance-theater works. Founded in 2011, DH had its world premiere in January 2012 at  The Kennedy Center  and has been presented by major venues throughout the US, including  Bard SummerScape, Brooklyn Academy of Music, Hopkins Center for the Arts, Jacob’s Pillow Dance Festival, The Joyce Theater, Lincoln Center, The Metropolitan Museum of Art,  and  Works Process at The Guggenheim,  among many others. DH has shared the stage with luminaries of the music world, including  Alarm Will Sound, Brooklyn Rider, The Knights, National Symphony Orchestra, Joshua Bell, André de Ridder,  and  Eric Jacobsen,  and has commissioned new scores from composers  Tyondai Braxton, Ethan Iverson,  and  Colin Jacobsen.  DH has collaborated with designers and artists  Maira Kalman, Isaac Mizrahi, Amy Trompetter, Maile Okamura,  and  Nicole Pearce i n the creation of new works. 
 www.danceheginbotham.org

title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
organization: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our  Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series , beginning  Monday, September 14 . 
 This  10-week workshop series  offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in  Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala  and are open to  students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University . No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. 
 Mondays, beginning September 14 5:30–7:30 p.m. Cole Hall, Room 141 10-week series 
 We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us.  Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: Accounting Society - KPMG
description: KPMG is a prominent global network of independent firms delivering professional audit, tax, and advisory services. As one of the prestigious "Big Four" accounting firms, it operates across roughly 140 countries and employs over 270,000 professionals worldwide. The organization was officially formed in 1987 through the merger of Peat Marwick International and Klynveld Main Goerdeler, with its name representing the initials of its foundational partners. Instead of functioning as a single multinational corporation, KPMG is structured as a network of distinct, locally managed member firms. Its primary client base includes major corporations, government agencies, and non-profit institutions seeking regulatory compliance and strategic business consulting. Through this decentralized model, the firm maintains a massive footprint in global financial compliance and corporate restructuring.

title: Information Session: Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group
description:
Are you a graduate student working on a journal article for publication? Learn more about the Grad Student Journal Article Writing Group! 
 This writing group will run over 13 weeks during the Spring semester (January - April 2027), with a week off in March. Weekly topics will include: publication venues, selecting a journal, writing your argument, literature review, citation management and more. We will use Wendy Laura Belcher’s  Writing Your Journal Article in Twelve Weeks  to guide the discussions and work.  
 Register to attend this Zoom information session where we will discuss how the program will run, the expected time commitment, and answer any other questions you may have. Please contact cwe@montclair.edu with any questions. A limited number of seats are available. 
 Sponsored by the Center for Writing Excellence and the University Libraries.

title: Chamber Opera Performance: "L'enfant et les Sortilèges"
description:
Maurice Ravel ’s  L’enfant et les sortilèges  is a wildly imaginative fantasy opera where a single child’s tantrum sets an entire enchanted world into motion. In a flash of frustration, the ordinary becomes extraordinary—walls start to whisper, teacups burst into song, animals argue back, and the child’s room transforms into a living, breathing world of magic and mischief. 
 As this fantastical realm awakens, the child is swept into a dazzling swirl of musical surprises and unexpected voices, where every object has something to say and nothing is quite as it seems. With Ravel’s shimmering, kaleidoscopic score at its heart, this enchanting opera is a playful journey through wonder, chaos, and the power of imagination to transform everything it touches. 
 (Sung in French with English Surtitles~ runtime: approx 1 hour) 
 Montclair State University Students  FREE  with ID at Kasser Box Office

title: Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers with New Jersey Hall of Fame
description:
Civic Leadership and SEL: Lessons from NJ Changemakers invites educators to explore how the powerful, personal stories of New Jersey Hall of Fame inductees can serve as catalysts for meaningful social-emotional learning and authentic civic engagement in today’s classrooms. By examining moments of courage, empathy, advocacy, and ethical decision-making in the lives of New Jersey leaders, educators will uncover practical ways to help students build self-awareness, social awareness, and a sense of agency. 
 Drawing from the lives and legacies of Peter J. McGuire (Father of Labor Day), Dorothea Dix (mental health reformer), David Mixner (political activist, author, and playwright), and Clara Maass (public health pioneer), participants will analyze how these changemakers confronted injustice, advocated for vulnerable communities, and took action in times of social and public health crises—making abstract concepts such as fairness, wellness, and justice tangible and relevant for students.  
 Educators will compare and contrast AI-powered lesson generators, including MagicSchool and Curipod, and create SEL or civic action lessons and student activities using inductee stories, leveraging AI scaffolding to differentiate instruction for diverse learners. This workshop empowers educators to transform local legends into catalysts for empathy, critical thinking, and civic participation—helping all students see themselves as the next generation of changemakers.

title: 2026 Class Gift Tabling - Information and Philanthropy Cord Pick-Up
description:
Each year, our graduating class participates in a proud Class Gift tradition where members of the class invest in the University by supporting areas of Montclair State University that are most important to them. We invite the Class of 2026 to come together to show your support! 
 All gifts to Montclair count! Make your gift to any area of campus you feel most passionate about – such as the Emergency Book Fund, The Red Hawk Pantry, your school or college, The Fund for Montclair State or athletic program. 
 Your gift will pay it forward for future Red Hawks and kick-start your philanthropic connection to Montclair. 
 
 Commemorate your class year! Make a gift of at least  $20.26  and you’ll receive your customized philanthropy cord to wear over your commencement robe.  
 For a gift of  $40 , celebrate this milestone with your family, friends and colleagues by having your message displayed on the screen at the Commencement you will be participating in, and receive a customized philanthropy cord. 
 
 How do I get my customized philanthropy cord? 
 Customized philanthropy cords will be available for pick-up: 
 
 Monday, October 26 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby 
 Thursday, November 2nd  from 2:00 – 4:00 p.m. in the Student Center Lobby 
 Tuesday, December 8 in the Student Center Lobby 
 
 Graduates can also arrange to pick up their philanthropy cords in the Overlook Corporate Center, 150 Clove Road, Little Falls, NJ during business hours, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. – 4:30 p.m. Philanthropy cords can also be mailed to those who cannot pick it up. Please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving at stewartj@montclair.edu or 973-655-5328 to finalize options to get your cords for the Winter Commencement. 
 Every student has benefitted from donor generosity to areas of academic support, emergency funding for students and overall priorities to boost students’ success every day. Thank you for paying it forward! For more information, please contact James Stewart, Associate Director of Annual Giving, at 973-655-5328 or stewartj@montclair.edu.

title: 2027 Legislative Breakfast: Human Trafficking, Online Exploitation & AI
description:
Registration is now open on eventbrite! 
 
 
 Elevate your education at our 5th Annual Legislative Breakfast, exploring human trafficking, online exploitation, AI, law, and policy. 
 Now in its fifth year, the  Legislative Breakfast: Addressing Human Trafficking: Law, Policy, and Practice  brings together policymakers, advocates, survivor leaders, researchers, students, and community members to advance meaningful dialogue and action on human trafficking law, policy, and practice. With nearly 200 attendees at last year’s event, the Legislative Breakfast continues to serve as an important forum for cross-sector engagement, collaboration, and action. 
 
 
 
 This year’s theme,  “Human Trafficking, Online Exploitation & Artificial Intelligence,”  examines how rapidly evolving technologies are reshaping the landscape of exploitation, from online recruitment and fraudulent schemes to AI-generated content and emerging digital threats. 
 Building on the success of previous years, the breakfast will bring together diverse perspectives to explore emerging challenges, share expertise, and identify opportunities for prevention, policy development, and cross-sector collaboration. Through an action-oriented discussion, participants will consider how law, policy, and practice can work together to address evolving forms of exploitation and strengthen prevention efforts.

title: Women's History Month Flag Raising & Reception
description:
Attention Montclair + Bloomfield Communities! 
   
 Get ready to raise the flag at the A&O annual Women's History Month flag raising and reception! 
 Join us Monday, March 1, 2027 to come together and honor the incredible achievements and ongoing impact of the women who make our campus community and world at large shine bright. 
 We'll begin with a special  flag raising ceremony at 12:30 PM in the Student Center Flag Pole  to collectively lift up the trailblazing women who have paved the way for us all. 
   
 Then, head over to the  Student Center Ballroom A&B  from 1:00 - 2:00 PM for a reception  you won't want to miss. We'll be mixing, mingling, eating, partying, crafting, and highlighting the talent, passion, and brilliance of the inspiring women in our midst. 
 This is your chance to celebrate, connect, and show some serious school spirit. Bring your energy, bring your pride, and get ready for an unforgettable afternoon! 
   
 Tell a friend to tell a friend. We can't wait to see you there!

 Set in a timeless, surreal Mediterranean landscape, "Phaedra" by Elizabeth Egloff is a reimagining of the classical myth that shifts the focus from grand public tragedy to a deeply personal experience of solitude, longing, and memory. The story is told by a mysterious Narrator who is haunted by the memory of Phaedra, a Queen paralyzed by a forbidden passion for her stepson, Hippolytus. As Phaedra languishes on her daybed, attended by her Nurse and observed by a chatty, opinionated Chorus, the world around her takes on a dreamlike quality where a sewing machine clatters with the rhythm of a heart and the landscape is an itemization of blue, leaving every character adrift in a sea of unrequited memory. When Phaedra finally breaks her silence to confront Hippolytus, her confession leads not to connection but to a psychic "emptying" of herself. The play concludes with the Narrator left in his own solitude, haunted by the echoes of those who have passed away. 
 
 Montclair State University Students:  FREE  tickets with ID at Kasser Box Office

title: Spring Dance
description:

title: Denim Day: Mind the Gaps, Move Forward
description:
April is Sexual Assault Awareness Month, and together, we can break the silence.  The Montclair State University Police Department and the Office of Advocacy & Outreach are committed to fostering a campus where survivors feel heard, supported, and empowered.  It starts with believing. It starts with you.  By offering a safe and affirming response to those who disclose gender-based and sexual violence, we can create lasting change. Let’s stand together to end the cycle of silence—because  every voice matters, and every action counts. 
 Denim Day is recognized internationally as a day of action and awareness, encouraging people to wear denim to challenge victim-blaming and educate others about sexual violence.  This year, Denim Day falls on Wednesday, April 28, 2027. 
 The University Police and  Office of Advocacy & Outreach and the Office of Advocacy and Community Resilience , in partnership with over 30 campus and local community organizations, invites you to join us  from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. at the Amphitheater  for a powerful awareness event honoring survivors and increasing awareness of available resources. 
 Despite the  gaps  that still exist in the criminal justice system, in resources, and in prevention education,  we will move forward together  as a community. As part of this commitment, we will walk  one mile around campus in solidarity with survivors.
